The per-head sparse pattern is looked up in `self.best_pattern`, which is loaded from the JSON file named by `config_path` in `init_minference_parameters` (lines 62-70). If the file is missing, or `self.layer_idx >= len(json.load(...))`, `best_pattern` is `{}` and every head silently gets the hard-coded default `("vertical_and_slash", 1000, 6096, 1)` instead of the searched pattern, so the sparse pattern actually used depends on the config file contents/length rather than on the input.
Config flag 'static_pattern' switches to vertical_and_slash_kernel_static, which caches the first computed vertical/slash indices in self.vs and reuses them for all later calls.
Config flag 'vs_only' forces the vertical_and_slash_kernel regardless of the per-head pattern type chosen from best_pattern.

In the vLLM path the pattern is indexed by `layer_idx` with no bounds check (unlike the HF path, which falls back to a default). A pattern config with fewer entries than the model has layers raises `IndexError` on the first forward of the extra layer, so the vLLM integration rejects models whose layer count exceeds the config's length.

`patch_hf` dispatches on the concrete model class: Llama/Mistral/Qwen2 get `LlamaAttention`-style patching, while MiniCPM/Phi3/ChatGLM are matched by class-name string and get their own patch functions. The same `attn_type` therefore maps to different patched forwards depending on the model class, and any other class falls through to the `ValueError` at line 1253.
